<a id="artisan-signatures"></a>
## artisan-signatures

Cosmetic pieces each crafting profession can sign. 'basis' says how solid the link is: 'crafted-variant' or 'signature-tag' means the catalog already marks the piece as a craftable variant or a signature item; 'proposed' means a static or stock-class piece with a clear craft fit that would need a new crafted variant. Carpentry (also instruments), tinkering (candelabras, lanterns, globes, goblets, clock) and blacksmithing (two suits of armor, a plate mannequin and bronze castings) have strong catalog support; tailoring, alchemy, cooking and inscription lean on 'proposed' pieces, and bowcraft has only two commons (the catalog has no rare fletching art). Owner decisions: whether a signed piece is a crafted copy of the base item or a reward for crafting milestones, and whether bowcraft needs new art. No NPC resale value, no stats.

<a id="bod-reward-tiers"></a>
## bod-reward-tiers

PROPOSAL ONLY: the actual BOD tier structure (how orders are issued, which crafts get which reward tier, how rewards are rolled) is a later roadmap item (Beta 3, BOD reward tiers) and is not decided here. This pool just proposes which cosmetic goes with which crafting profession at three tiers: 'small' (plain workshop pieces and goods), 'large' (fuller pieces) and 'exceptional' (the best-looking piece of that craft), using catalog tiers common, uncommon and scarce-to-rare to line up. Eight crafts are covered: blacksmithing, carpentry, tailoring, tinkering, alchemy, cooking, bowcraft and inscription. Weak spots: bowcraft has only commons in the catalog (the exceptional is an arrow-slit wall) and cooking and inscription share a few 'exceptional' pieces. These pieces are kept separate from artisan-signatures, so a BOD reward and a crafted signature are never the same design. Cosmetic only; no NPC resale or BOD-value, as for all catalog rewards.

<a id="camping-rewards"></a>
## camping-rewards

Fifteen pieces for a Rekindled camp, all grade B or better and almost all tagged 'camp'. 'kind' says which outcome they suit: hearth (what a campfire can leave behind), shelter, bedding, provisions and trail (relics left along a route). Catalog tiers run from common (kindling, a campfire, a bedroll) up to the whole Hunter's Camp as the extremely-rare showpiece, so the humblest camping outcome is a small, useful-looking keepsake and the rarest is a full camp tableau. Other camp-tagged pieces (extra tents, the camp kitchen, skinner's and hunter's poles, tool and cookware sets) are held back on purpose for the artisan and BOD pools, so the camping set stays about the fire, the bedroll and the trail.

<a id="hot-zone-drops"></a>
## hot-zone-drops

Rare cosmetic drops from Hot Zone monsters and chests (Hythloth has its own pool). Five themes so the loot matches the killer: undead and graveyard (sarcophagi, coffins), bones and candles, dragon hoards, shadowiron and dark relics, and dark arcana (rite tables, grimoires, bloody altars). 'tier' is the catalog tier and can be used as drop rarity (three extremely-rare: the ornate sarcophagus, the dragon's hoard and the twin bloodstained altars). 'theme' lets a system roll from the right group (undead corpse, dragon corpse, chest). Three entries are era grade C: the dragon hoards are the only hoard art of that kind in the catalog, and the pool would feel hollow without them. Nothing here is mentioned as a Nemesis trophy, a Wanted curator item or a shipwreck piece.

<a id="hythloth-drops"></a>
## hythloth-drops

Hythloth is the permanent Hot dungeon, so its drops are the most hellish pieces in the catalog: two daemon figures, the Blood Pentagram, the dungeon arch the catalog tags 'dungeon:hythloth', demon faces, a blood altar and a skull wreathed in fire. 'tier' is the catalog tier and can be used directly as drop rarity (five extremely-rare, so the top end is always a daemon or a hell-gate piece). 'theme' groups the pieces so a daemon corpse can roll daemon items and a chest can roll rite items. One piece (CR-CUR-019) is era grade C: kept because nothing else in the catalog reads as hellfire this clearly. Hythloth is not a Wanted destination, so none of these overlap the curator pools.

<a id="nemesis-species-trophies"></a>
## nemesis-species-trophies

Plan 6.1: one species trophy per species, identical everywhere. Monster figurines (FIG) are used wherever the species has one, because a figurine is the clearest possible species link (owner rule 2026-10-08: a figurine is fine when its creature is present in our game; every figurine species here is spawned by the shard, see Species-In-Game.md). Species with no figurine use lair pieces that evoke them: orc captain and orc lord take the rust-red war banners, the mummy a sarcophagus, the black bear a bearskin rug. 52 species. Still without a main-catalog figurine (the era-neutral section has some, ids CN-FIG-...): imp, orcish mage, wyvern, ancient wyrm, kraken, hell hound and the other dungeon creatures; using era-neutral ids in pools needs an owner decision. Gazer and giant spider rest on grade C art (their creature dates are unverified), and the drake reuses the jade dragon figurine, so it looks like a dragon; the owner may prefer to drop those three.

<a id="pilgrimage-shrine-tokens"></a>
## pilgrimage-shrine-tokens

One green-marble virtue mosaic per shrine, each carrying that virtue's own golden emblem (hand, heart, scales, sword, chalice, flame, ankh, crook), so the eight tokens read as one collectible set and each is unmistakable at a glance. All are grade B, tradable floor pieces with no function. The ninth entry, the Ring of the Eight Virtues, is an optional capstone for a pilgrim who has visited every shrine: it is the same eight emblems joined in a circle, listed under 'singularity' (the unity of the virtues). Drop it and the pool still satisfies 'one token per shrine'. There is no separate art for 'Spirit'. Which towns host which shrine, and whether the curator trades tokens for the Ring, is a Pilgrimage design matter for the roadmap item, not decided here.

## seasonal-halloween

Hallows' Eve pool (season:halloween): grinning jack-o'-lanterns, a witch's cauldron over coals, webs, gibbets and a churchyard. IMPORTANT: the era evidence found no Halloween items documented before 2006, so seven of these fifteen pieces are era grade C (the whole SEA Halloween set) and the pool is flavour for an event rather than a period claim; the owner may prefer to drop or delay it. The grade B pieces (graves, coffins, sheeted chair, moth-eaten bed, black candle, stopped clock) do exist in the era as dungeon and graveyard dressing and reuse that art for the event. ## seasonal-winter

Winter holiday pool (season:winter): holiday trees and Yule hearth pieces up top, frosted trees and snow in the middle, small seasonal touches at the bottom. 'tier' is the catalog tier and can be used as event drop rarity (the Classic Holiday Tree, which the era evidence documents as a December 1998 and 1999 holiday gift, is the single extremely-rare). Most of the snow and ice crags went to the Ice curator and the Nemesis pool, so this set leans on holiday trees, frosted trees and Yule fire. The Little Snowman (CR-SEA-014) is deliberately left out: the era notes put its art in the 2003 winter package. Every piece here is grade A or B. Winter art has no function; whether these are event drops, a vendor's seasonal stock or both is for the Retention roadmap item.

<a id="shipwreck-decor"></a>
## shipwreck-decor

One weighted roll per salvaged wreck, so the art runs from flotsam (lantern, crate, cask, driftwood) through a captain's cabin (chest, chart and sextant) to hull pieces (anchor, cannon, strongbox) and one showpiece, the Lighthouse Lamp Room, which the catalog already tags shipwreck. The longboat section (CR-NAU-042) is the most wreck-like piece of all but is grade C, so it is left out; swap it in for the cannon if the owner would rather have it.

<a id="wanted-curator-covetous"></a>
## wanted-curator-covetous

Covetous is greed in a dungeon, so the set is bones, webs and the treasure that killed their owners. Tiers climb from a skull to silver chests to the Golden Pylon, a gold-sheathed miniature tomb that is the showpiece. The skull-on-gold and dragon hoards are held by the Hot Zone pool and the Bullion Vault by the Minoc expedition.
